raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Enable Bolt E4B serving with breakable prefill CUDA graphs, including image inputs for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16`. The fix also applies to Gemma4. These models share KV caches between layers, but graph setup needs a separate execution ID for each layer.

Breakable prefill graphs are the default for the text-only path used by the separate Bolt E4B Q4_K_M GGUF target PR, which needs this fix for default startup. For multimodal Gemma4/Bolt BF16, prefill graphs remain disabled by default; use `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` to opt in. This PR leaves those defaults unchanged.

During validation of the newly enabled graph path, three of eight image checks failed for both Bolt E4B BF16 and Gemma4, while eager execution passed. Multimodal embedding preparation changed the token IDs needed for per-layer embedding lookup during graph replay. Preserving those IDs restores the expected image answers.

## Modifications

- Add an optional graph execution ID to `RadixAttention` and use it when indexing layers for prefill graphs.
- Supply each Gemma4 attention layer's execution ID while keeping its KV-cache owner ID unchanged.
- Accept graph-supplied embeddings alongside IDs used for per-layer lookup.
- Preserve image token IDs before multimodal embedding preparation changes them.
- Add graph-indexing and image-input regressions. Multimodal prefill graph defaults stay unchanged.

Existing callers keep using `layer_id` unless they supply a graph ID. This PR applies the separation to Gemma4, including Bolt E4B; other models remain unchanged. Pipeline padding, repeated-layer handling, and duplicate validation are preserved.

## Accuracy Tests

Bolt E4B BF16 and Gemma4 E4B each passed eight image checks plus a text control with breakable prefill graphs on H100 and Blackwell (SM103). Checks covered colors, positions, counting, OCR, and two-image ordering. Before the token-ID fix, three image checks failed.

H100 used Triton, matching its architecture default. Blackwell left attention options unset and selected `trtllm_mha`; eager controls also passed both models' checks. Each breakable run logged ten graphed prefills and zero eager prefills, including warmup. The default TRTLLM backend warns that it uses causal image attention, so these smoke checks do not establish full vision accuracy.

At main base `1d605b7e` plus this PR, all nine focused CPU tests and full pre-commit passed in Docker, including Rust. The image regression was verified red/green, with 64% changed-line coverage. Validated text and image inputs at TP1. Bolt E4B BF16 also passed all nine text/image smoke checks at TP2 on two H100 NVL GPUs, using default Triton attention with eager and breakable prefill. Answers matched; the breakable run recorded ten graphed prefills and no eager fallback, including warmup.

Full prefill remains unsupported for the tested image path. Triton and default TRTLLM fail capture; H100 FA4 falls back to eager for images, and Blackwell FA4 encounters kernel restrictions before image requests. This PR's image graph results use breakable prefill.

The latest Bolt image run used the public revision below.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16 \
  --revision 49843eed8db1f1c616c47af75cfd36e07aec0667 \
  --served-model-name bolt-e4b \
  --context-length 8192 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --max-total-tokens 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 \
  --reasoning-parser gemma4 --random-seed 42 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable --watchdog-timeout 900
```

For TP2, append `--tp-size 2` to the command above.

Leave attention options unset to use the architecture default. Use `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` to exercise the fixed path. Image requests used `/v1/chat/completions`, base64 PNGs, temperature 0, `max_tokens=128`, and `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`.

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/models/test_gemma4_mm.py
python3 test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_cuda_graph_setup.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One H100 and one B200, TP1, with default attention (Triton and `trtllm_mha`). Compared upstream eager, branch eager, and branch breakable prefill; decode graphs stayed enabled.

Text used 1,024 input tokens before template overhead. Images used 256 text tokens plus one random 512×512 PNG. Outputs were fixed at 64 tokens, thinking disabled. Three runs per setting, 20 requests at concurrency 1 and 40 at concurrency 4, four warmups and cache flushing after warmup. Values below are medians of three runs; TTFT uses each run's mean.

The table below compares eager vs breakable-graph execution on this PR branch:

| GPU | Input | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms), eager → graphs | Output tokens/s, eager → graphs |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H100 | Text | 1 | 52.8 → 30.9 | 144.6 → 151.5 |
| H100 | Text | 4 | 104.3 → 74.2 | 498.7 → 517.3 |
| H100 | Image | 1 | 101.6 → 73.3 | 131.1 → 139.3 |
| H100 | Image | 4 | 203.7 → 154.6 | 418.9 → 447.0 |
| B200 | Text | 1 | 41.5 → 19.3 | 208.1 → 233.0 |
| B200 | Text | 4 | 78.7 → 41.0 | 733.4 → 806.6 |
| B200 | Image | 1 | 82.0 → 55.1 | 183.9 → 206.2 |
| B200 | Image | 4 | 165.9 → 112.6 | 581.3 → 655.9 |

All 2,160 measured requests succeeded, and all measured prefills in graph mode replayed graphs. B200 uses the existing causal image-attention fallback noted above. Small synthetic benchmarks; no profiling performed.


Use the same local checkpoint path as the served name so the image benchmark can find its processor. For the upstream eager baseline, use base `1d605b7e` with prefill disabled; on this branch, compare disabled and breakable. Keep the benchmark client source the same.

```bash
model_dir=$(hf download nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-BF16 \
  --revision 49843eed8db1f1c616c47af75cfd36e07aec0667)
prefill=breakable  # Use disabled for eager prefill.

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$model_dir" --served-model-name "$model_dir" \
  --context-length 8192 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --max-total-tokens 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill "$prefill" \
  --random-seed 42 --watchdog-timeout 900
```

In another terminal, set `model_dir` to the same checkpoint directory. Run each server configuration from a separate output directory:

```bash
for seed in 42 43 44; do
  for dataset in random image; do
    input_len=1024
    image_args=()
    if [ "$dataset" = image ]; then
      input_len=256
      image_args=(--image-count 1 --image-resolution 512x512
                  --image-format png --image-content random)
    fi
    for concurrency in 1 4; do
      requests=20
      if [ "$concurrency" = 4 ]; then requests=40; fi
      python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
        --backend sglang-oai-chat --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30001 \
        --model "$model_dir" --tokenizer "$model_dir" \
        --dataset-name "$dataset" "${image_args[@]}" \
        --random-input-len "$input_len" --random-output-len 64 \
        --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts "$requests" \
        --max-concurrency "$concurrency" --warmup-requests 4 \
        --flush-cache --seed "$seed" --temperature 0 \
        --extra-request-body '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}' \
        --cache-report --output-details --disable-tqdm \
        --output-file "${dataset}-c${concurrency}-s${seed}.jsonl"
    done
  done
done
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: Low**

**Issue**

Gemma3n shares KV caches the same way, but this PR sets `graph_layer_id` only for Gemma4. In `gemma3n_causal.py` (line 416), each KV-shared layer still passes the owner's index as `layer_id` and passes no `graph_layer_id`. `index_attention_layers_by_global_id` then sees two layers with one ID and raises `invalid or duplicate attention layer_id`.

**Example**

`Gemma3nForCausalLM` is not multimodal, so breakable prefill graphs are on by default on CUDA. Startup would fail at graph setup, the same way Gemma4 text did before this PR.

**Fix**

Pass `graph_layer_id=layer_id` to `RadixAttention` in `Gemma3nAttention`. If Gemma3n is out of scope, say so in the PR description.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

`test_graph_id_tracks_cache_id_when_no_execution_id_is_set` passes on the base commit, so it does not guard this change. The duplicate case in `test_shared_kv_layers_keep_distinct_graph_entries` already covers the fallback to `layer_id` when no graph ID is set. `test_pipeline_attention_metadata_is_indexed_by_global_layer_id` already covers padding to a higher ID. The only extra check is that a later change to `layer_id` is seen, and no model changes `layer_id` without also setting `graph_layer_id`.

**Fix**

Delete this test, per `.claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md`.
